status.en: 8 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 62% fewer than the week before, most of them in La Espriella, Planadas and Bogota.
status.nb: 8 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 62 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i La Espriella, Planadas og Bogota.

summary.en: Colombia rejected a U.S. proposal for joint anti-drug strikes while President Petro was accused of freezing purchases of equipment to counter armed-group drones. A Trump-backed right-wing lawyer appears to have won the presidential election, and the government secured the release of two ELN hostages through a deal with Venezuela. U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth arrived in Bogotá to reinforce the security agenda. In Kyiv, a 19‑year-old woman was detained for poisoning a Colombian veteran of the Ukrainian Armed Forces for $1,000. The conflict recorded 225 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Colombia avviste et amerikansk forslag om felles anti-narkotikastridder mens president Petro ble anklaget for å fryse innkjøp av utstyr for å motvirke væpnede gruppers droner. En høyreadvokat støttet av Trump ser ut til å ha vunnet presidentvalget, og regjeringen sikret løslatelsen av to ELN-gisler gjennom en avtale med Venezuela. USAs forsvarsminister Pete Hegseth ankom Bogotá for å styrke sikkerhetsagendaen. I Kyiv ble en 19‑år gammel kvinne pågrepet for å ha forgiftet en colombiansk veteran fra de ukrainske væpnede styrkene for 1 000 dollar. Konflikten registrerte 225 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
